state.question: Has Estuary Works's operating change resolved the question about water quality compliance? Focus on: September compliant drinking-water samples as a share of tested samples under the same limit.
state.gap: September compliant drinking-water samples as a share of tested samples under the same limit.

candidates.title: Estuary Works: what the announcement changes
candidates.abstract: Our reporting desk follows Estuary Works, drawing on an independent correspondent's account of september compliant drinking-water samples as a share of tested samples under the same limit.

candidates.title: Estuary Works: the operating record
candidates.abstract: Estuary Works features in a field guide to water quality compliance. The worked example draws on a separate setting: an equipment catalogue lists compliance badges without sample results.

candidates.title: Estuary Works: the strategic argument
candidates.abstract: A commentary revisiting Estuary Works's operating announcement, carrying the same factual account as the public record.

candidates.title: Estuary Works: the latest field dispatch
candidates.abstract: I set out the case for Estuary Works's strategy in water quality compliance, using incentives and managerial judgement to project the next stage.

candidates.title: Estuary Works: the weekly notebook
candidates.abstract: Estuary accredited laboratory return supports a dated assessment of september compliant drinking-water samples as a share of tested samples under the same limit.

candidates.title: Estuary Works: the briefing behind the numbers
candidates.abstract: An edited digest of Inez Rao's Dispatch's dispatch on Estuary Works, retaining its reported comparison and attribution.
